h1:
Bangkok Cafe Hopping: 3-Day Plan
Charoen Krung · Ari · Thong Lor
intro: Bangkok is a serious specialty-coffee city, with hundreds of small-batch roasters spread across neighborhoods that each have their own clear character. We've put together a 3-day plan for cafe hoppers across three of the best districts. Day one is Charoen Krung and Talat Noi along the Chao Phraya River, day two is laid-back Ari with its leafy sois, and day three closes out in hip Thong Lor. Every shop here is open right now, you can walk between them, and we give you honest ballpark prices.

blocks.html: The fun of cafe hopping in Bangkok is that every district feels different. Charoen Krung is old riverside buildings that have turned into a cluster of cafes and galleries. Ari is a quiet residential neighborhood with plenty of small roasters tucked down the sois. Thong Lor is the hip, slightly pricier district where the coffee quality is consistently strong. This plan keeps each day walkable, so you're not crossing the city by car every hour.

blocks.title: Read this before you head out
blocks.html: Most specialty cafes open late, around 9–10am, and close around 5–6pm. Some are closed on Mondays or Tuesdays. Always check the shop's page before you go, especially for the tiny spots in Talat Noi.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Charoen Krung · Talat Noi · Song Wat

blocks.html: This area is heaven for anyone who loves coffee and old buildings. You can walk along the Chao Phraya River from Charoen Krung into Talat Noi and on to Song Wat in a single day, with the shops lined up within walking distance. Take the river boat or the MRT to Hua Lamphong station and walk straight into the sois.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Coffee crawl along the Chao Phraya

items.note: A cafe-and-brunch spot in a warehouse close to 150 years old. They roast their own beans, the coffee is strong for both espresso and drip, and the breakfast is properly done. Coffee around ฿110–150.

items.activity: Walk into Talat Noi and stop at Mother Roaster
items.note: A tiny shop where the owner, an older lady, slow-drips coffee in an old riverside building. Lovely vintage setting for photos. Drip coffee around ฿120–160. Few seats, so be ready to queue.

items.activity: Break for lunch in Talat Noi
items.note: This area has roast-duck rice, noodles, and old Chinese eateries, all findable in the same lane.

items.activity: Move to Song Wat for Beans Coffee Roasters (Song Wat branch)
items.note: They roast their own single-origin beans and do a careful V60 plus solid espresso in an old shophouse. Coffee around ฿90–140.

items.activity: Finish at Local Boys Coffee Co, Song Wat
items.note: A garage-style shop with graffiti and bold, full-on coffee. Great for anyone who likes a heavy roast. Around ฿120–160.

items.activity: Wander and shoot photos by the river before heading back
items.note: The evening light is lovely, and Song Wat–Talat Noi is a relaxed stretch for photographing old buildings.

blocks.title: Day-one tip
blocks.html: Many shops in Talat Noi have very few seats. If you're in a group or it's a weekend, go in the morning before the crowds and leave extra time to queue at Mother Roaster.

blocks.html: Ari is a residential neighborhood that has become a cafe hub, with shops hidden down the small sois. It's an easy walk from BTS Ari into the various lanes. The area is known for champion-level roasters and pretty garden cafes where you can settle in and work for hours.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Taking it slow in the Ari sois

items.activity: Open the morning at Nana Coffee Roasters Ari
items.note: A team of national-level champion baristas and roasters. The space feels like a glasshouse in a garden, with a slow bar where you can pick from a range of beans. Coffee around ฿150–250, and they do brunch too.
The area has plenty of Thai restaurants, noodle shops, and Western eateries, all within walking distance.
One of Bangkok's specialty-coffee heavyweights. They roast Thai beans themselves and focus on coffee from Thai farmers, with a clean cup and clear tasting notes. Coffee around ฿110–160.

items.activity: Settle in to work at Porcupine Café
items.note: A warm, wooden-cabin-style shop with lots of outlets, good for a long sit. Try the flat white at ฿120 with the carrot cake at ฿140.

items.activity: Close out the photo run at Glig Cafe
items.note: A minimal, clean Korean-style spot that photographs beautifully. The standout is the Iced Einspänner with its soft cream at ฿150. Expect to spend around ฿120–180.

blocks.title: Day-two tip
blocks.html: Ari is more walkable than you'd think, but the midday sun is strong, so bring an umbrella or walk in the morning and late afternoon. Big names like Nana and Roots get busy on weekends; if you can go on a weekday, you'll get a more comfortable seat.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Thong Lor, the hip district

blocks.html: Thong Lor runs a bit pricier, but the coffee quality is strong and the shops are well designed. You can walk along Sukhumvit 55 (Thong Lor) or grab a motorbike taxi deeper into the sois. The center of gravity for coffee fans is theCOMMONS, an open-air community mall that gathers good shops in one place.

items.activity: Start at Roots theCOMMONS Thong Lor
items.note: The original Roots location in a lively, open-air community space. Try the pineapple cold brew or the espresso tonic. Coffee around ฿110–170.
There are dessert shops, bakeries, and snacks to stop at, all in one building. You can sit in the open-air zone upstairs.
Thong Lor has loads of Japanese, Thai, and fusion restaurants. Take your pick within walking distance.

items.activity: Find another cafe to relax in down the Thong Lor sois
items.note: The area has stylish, well-designed cafes scattered through the side lanes. Stroll and pick one you like for a long afternoon sit.

items.activity: End the trip with dessert or one last coffee
items.note: Before heading back, find a dessert cafe to finish on, then hop the BTS at Thong Lor for an easy ride home.

items: Specialty coffee — around ฿90–250 a cup depending on the shop and the drink. Thong Lor and Nana run a bit higher.
Hopping 4–5 shops a day — roughly ฿500–900 per person, including coffee and a few small snacks.
Transport — MRT/BTS at ฿20–60 per ride. On day one, the Chao Phraya river boat is cheaper.

blocks.text: Tricks to make cafe hopping more fun

items: Don't order a big cup at every shop. Go for espresso or a small black coffee so you can try more places without filling up.
Drink plain water between shops. Several cups of coffee in one day can leave you jittery if you don't.
Many small shops are cash-only or prefer PromptPay, so keep some cash on you.
If you want to work, pick a shop with outlets and plenty of seats like Porcupine. The tiny shops in Talat Noi are better for a quick photo stop before moving on.

faq.q: Which district should I start cafe hopping in Bangkok?
faq.a: If you have 3 days, start with Charoen Krung–Talat Noi, since the shops are lined up along the river and easy to walk. Then move on to leafy Ari, and finish in hip Thong Lor. If you only have one day, pick Charoen Krung or Ari, where the shops are easiest to reach on foot.

faq.q: How much does specialty coffee cost in Bangkok?
faq.a: Most cups run around ฿90–250. Typical small roasters are about ฿100–160, while big names like Nana Coffee Roasters or shops in Thong Lor climb to ฿150–250 a cup.

faq.q: What time do Bangkok cafes open?
faq.a: Most specialty cafes open late, around 9–10am, and close around 5–6pm. Some are closed on Mondays or Tuesdays. Check the shop's page before you go, especially for the small spots in Talat Noi.

faq.q: Can I do a Bangkok cafe trip without a car?
faq.a: Easily. All three districts are close to the train lines. For Charoen Krung–Talat Noi, take the MRT to Hua Lamphong or the Chao Phraya river boat. For Ari, take BTS Ari, and for Thong Lor, BTS Thong Lor. From the stations you can walk straight into the sois to the shops.

faq.q: How many cafes can I do in one day?
faq.a: Around 4–5 shops a day is doable if you order small cups and leave time to walk. Don't order a big cup everywhere or you'll be too full and over-caffeinated. Drinking plain water between shops helps.
